evidence.fact: Mazamas lists elevation gain of 5,400 ft for Shuksan via the White Salmon Glacier.

facts.value: Shorter, more direct alternative to the Fisher Chimneys route, but the approach can be choked with brush

evidence.fact: Mazamas: an alternative to Fisher Chimneys, shorter and more direct but guarded by punishing brush.

facts.value: Series of small glaciers descending north from the Shuksan Arm; climbers follow it to Fisher Chimney as a faster approach

evidence.fact: Wikipedia: small glaciers flowing north from Shuksan Arm; a climbers' route follows it to Fisher Chimney, faster than others.

facts.value: Early season, about mid-June in normal snow years, for the easiest passage; graded for spring and summer

evidence.fact: Mazamas: go early (mid June in most normal years) for easiest passage; rated C in spring and summer.

facts.value: Car to car in two or more days

evidence.fact: Mazamas expected duration: car to car in two or more days.

wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.note: Mazamas gain 5,400 ft vs app 7,500 ft; single source, not reconciled.

evidence.fact: The Mountaineers lists elevation gain 5,250 ft for the West Ridge.
The Mountaineers lists high point 9,415 ft.

facts.value: Northwest Forest Pass

evidence.fact: Mountaineers: parking requires a Northwest Forest Pass; land manager Okanogan-Wenatchee NF, Alpine Lakes Wilderness.

facts.value: End of North Fork Teanaway road (4,243 ft), about 23 mi up from SR-970

evidence.fact: Mountaineers: I-90 exit 85, SR-970 6.6 mi, Teanaway River Road, north fork road about 23 mi to the end at 4,243 ft.

facts.value: Trail to Ingalls Pass (6,480 ft) and Ingalls Lake, down to Ingalls Creek and over it on a log bridge; some go via Long's Pass instead

evidence.fact: Mountaineers: Ingalls Pass 6,480 ft to Ingalls Lake, down to Ingalls Creek and cross on a log; some take Long's Pass.

facts.value: From the upper Ingalls Creek meadows, short of Stuart Pass, climb to the base of the West Ridge

evidence.fact: Mountaineers: at the upper Ingalls Creek meadows below Stuart Pass, ascend to the West Ridge base.

facts.value: Meadows near the head of Ingalls Creek; most parties carry over with a bivy near the summit

evidence.fact: Mountaineers: some overnight in upper Ingalls Creek meadows; most carry over and bivy near the summit.

facts.value: Middle of three parallel gullies (house-sized boulder at its base) to a notch, chimney left of Long John Tower, ledges right of the west ridge tower, benches below the crest to the West Ridge Notch, class 4 blocks to the summit

evidence.fact: Mountaineers ascent: middle boulder gully, chimney by Long John Tower, ledges south of the tower, benches to West Ridge Notch, class 4 blocks.

facts.value: Scramble to the false summit, down steep snow or scree, trend right through trees into the Cascadian Couloir to the valley; Ingalls Creek Trail west to the Long's Pass / Ingalls Lake fork

evidence.fact: Mountaineers descent: false summit, then Cascadian Couloir to the valley floor, west on Ingalls Creek Trail to the Long's Pass or Ingalls Lake fork.

facts.value: Trailhead to climb 4-6 hr; to Long John Tower 4 hr; to West Rib Notch 4-5 hr; to summit 4-6 hr; summit to trailhead 7 hr

evidence.fact: Mountaineers trip profile: TH to climb 4-6 h, to Long John Tower 4, to West Rib Notch 4-5, to summit 4-6, summit to TH 7.

facts.value: Trailhead to climb 2,500; to Long John Tower 1,000; to West Rib Notch 350; to summit 400; summit to trailhead 1,000

evidence.fact: Mountaineers trip profile gain per segment: 2,500 / 1,000 / 350 / 400 / 1,000 ft.

facts.value: Small rack to two inches; ice axe in early season

evidence.fact: Mountaineers equipment: small rack to 2 inches, ice axe early season.

facts.value: Route-finding trouble spots: Long John Tower and the exposed West Ridge Notch section

evidence.fact: Mountaineers notes route-finding dilemmas at Long John Tower and the exposed West Ridge Notch.
